about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hollister, California
about.longDescription: Hollister sits at the heart of San Benito County, where local roads like 4th Street, San Felipe Road, Rt 25, and San Benito Street carry residents through daily errands, farm work, and weekend trips. Public records show 104 injury collisions in the most recent year, leaving 144 people hurt — a reminder that even a routine drive across town can turn into a life-altering event. If you or someone you love was injured in a crash, a fall, or another accident in Hollister, sorting out next steps while dealing with pain, missed work, and medical bills can feel overwhelming. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't provide legal advice ourselves — we simply help you find someone who can. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You don't have to figure this out alone or guess at deadlines. Reaching out costs nothing, and it may help you understand what your situation is worth before time runs short.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: Your Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so acting sooner matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages, so compensation for pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency, which means there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Exploring your options costs nothing out of pocket.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Hollister?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government entity or vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's wise to look into your options early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Hollister?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors such as 4th Street, San Felipe Road, Rt 25, and San Benito Street, with reported crashes tending to peak on Saturdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a recovery. There's no cost to reach out and learn where you stand.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specifics of your injury and case, which an attorney can help evaluate.
